title: Topological Transverse Transport without a Gap in Critical Topological Flat Bands
authors: Chang-geun Oh, Tomoki Ozawa, Jun-Won Rhim
abstract: Quantized Hall transport is traditionally anchored to a bulk spectral gap, which isolates the occupied subspace and exponentially suppresses thermal deviations. Recently discovered critical topological flat bands (CTFBs) challenge this paradigm: an exactly flat band touches a dispersive continuum while retaining a well-defined integer Chern number. However, their finite-temperature transverse transport properties remain entirely unexplored. Here, we develop a low-temperature theory of the intrinsic electrical, thermoelectric, and thermal Hall responses in CTFBs. At fixed particle number, the macroscopic flat-band degeneracy forces a singular Lambert-$W$ drift of the chemical potential, generating an algebraic-logarithmic hierarchy of low-temperature corrections: $T\ln(1/T)$ for electrical Hall, $T[\ln(1/T)]^2$ for thermoelectric Hall, and $T[\ln(1/T)]^3$ for thermal Hall conductivity, replacing the activated thermal protection of a gapped Chern insulator. By contrast, externally pinning the chemical potential to the flat-band energy locks the flat band to half occupation at any nonzero temperature, obstructing the recovery of the fully filled topological ground state as $T\to0^+$. Our results establish that a bulk spectral gap is unnecessary for zero-temperature Hall quantization, but indispensable for its exponential thermal protection.
summary: This work analyzes the thermal transport in Critical Topological Flat Bands (CTFBs), showing that these systems maintain quantized Hall conductivity at zero temperature without a spectral gap. However, the absence of a gap leads to algebraic-logarithmic temperature corrections rather than the exponential suppression seen in gapped insulators. This establishes a critical distinction between the requirements for zero-temperature quantization versus thermal stability.
main_problem: The paper investigates the finite-temperature transverse transport properties of Critical Topological Flat Bands (CTFBs), challenging the traditional requirement of a bulk spectral gap for quantized Hall transport.
main_result: CTFBs show an algebraic-logarithmic hierarchy of low-temperature corrections ($T\ln(1/T)$, etc.), demonstrating that while a gap is unnecessary for zero-temperature quantization, it remains indispensable for exponential thermal protection.
method: The authors developed a low-temperature theory using the cumulative Chern weight and analyzed the system under fixed particle number constraints to derive the temperature dependence of Hall responses.
model_or_system: The study focuses on CTFBs, which are characterized by an exactly flat band touching a dispersive continuum while maintaining an integer Chern number. The analysis uses a lattice model (e.g., the 2pi-fluxed dice lattice) to calculate transport coefficients.
key_observables: Electrical, thermoelectric, and thermal Hall responses ($\sigma_{xy}, \alpha_{xy}, \kappa_{xy}/T$), and the chemical potential $\mu(T)$.
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), the spectral gap ($\Delta$), and the characteristic energy scales related to residual dispersion ($W_f$) and disorder ($\Gamma$).
main_assumptions: The fixed particle number condition is crucial, leading to a singular Lambert-W drift of the chemical potential; the analysis also compares results to the grand-canonical ensemble.
figures_summary: Figures compare the band structure and cumulative Chern weight for gapped vs. CTFB systems, and show the temperature dependence of transport coefficients for both lattice calculations and continuum theory.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework by comparing gapped Chern insulators to CTFBs, derives the low-temperature expansions for the CTFB under fixed particle number, contrasts this with the grand-canonical case, and discusses the implications for thermal protection.
why_interesting: The findings provide a detailed, quantitative understanding of how topological protection breaks down in gapless systems, offering insights into non-equilibrium thermal transport in strongly correlated or topological materials.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic comparison of a gapped Chern insulator and a critical topological flat band. (a) Band structure of a gapped Chern insulator with a spectral gap ∆= Ec −Ev separating the valence and conduction bands. (b) Band structure of a CTFB system, where an exactly flat band at Ef (blue) touches an upper dispersive band (red) quadratically at a single momentum point. (c,d) Cumulative Chern weight C(E) for (c) Chern insulator and (d) CTFB system. Here, C is an integer.

FIG. 2. Lattice model verification of the critical topology flat-band continuum theory. (a) Band structure of the fluxed dice-lattice model in Eq. (15). (b) Cumulative Chern weight C(E). (c)–(f) The temperature T dependence of the fixed-filling chemical potential µ, electric Hall σxy, thermoelectric Hall αxy, and thermal Hall (κxy/T) coefficients. Red circles denote the results from lattice calculations, while solid curves are the low-energy continuum results in Eqs. (10) and (13) with D0 and eΩ0 determined from the lattice model.
